name: Chicken & Turkey
summary: White meat vs. dark meat, cooking each part, whole birds, spatchcocking, and turkey basics.

sections.heading: White meat vs. dark meat
blocks: **Breast** (white meat) is lean and mild, and turns dry and stringy soon after it's done. Cook it to 165°F (74°C) and no further.

**Thighs and legs** (dark meat) have more fat and connective tissue, so they stay juicy and forgiving. They're safe at 165°F (74°C) but get more tender cooked to about 175–185°F (79–85°C), which is why roast chicken legs taste better than the breast.

blocks.text: All poultry, including ground chicken and turkey, must reach 165°F (74°C). Don't rinse raw poultry: it spreads bacteria around the sink. See [Doneness & Food Safety](guide:doneness-and-food-safety).

rows: Pound thick ends to an even thickness so it cooks evenly, or slice it in half horizontally into cutlets.
Bone and skin keep it juicier than boneless.
The most forgiving piece. Skin-on thighs roasted hot get very crisp.

sections.heading: Spatchcocking
blocks: Cutting out the backbone and flattening a whole bird makes it cook faster and more evenly, with all the skin facing up to crisp.

items: Put the bird breast side down. With sturdy kitchen shears, cut along both sides of the backbone and remove it (save it for stock).
Turn it over and press firmly on the breastbone with the heel of your hand until it cracks and lies flat.
Roast at 425–450°F (220–230°C): a 4 lb (1.8 kg) chicken takes about 40–50 minutes. Check the thigh and the breast.
**Size:** allow about 1–1 ½ lb (450–700 g) of whole turkey per person, more if you want leftovers.
**Thawing:** in the fridge, about a day for every 4–5 lb (2 kg). A 16 lb (7 kg) turkey needs about 4 days. See [thawing safely](guide:doneness-and-food-safety#thawing).
**Roasting:** 325°F (160°C) is the usual temperature; an unstuffed 12–14 lb (5.5–6.5 kg) turkey takes roughly 3–3 ¾ hours. Go by the thermometer, not the clock.
**Done:** 165°F (74°C) in the thickest part of the breast and in the thigh, then rest 20–30 minutes before carving.
**Stuffing:** baking it in a separate dish is safer and the turkey cooks faster. If it's inside the bird, the stuffing's center must also reach 165°F (74°C).
